copy.failed: Copy failed. Select the text instead

date_picker.outside: That day is outside what can be chosen.
date_picker.not_a_day: That is not a day. Try {example} or 2026-10-05.

desktop_nav.pin_hint: Point at a page and press its pin to keep it here.

sidebar.label: Sidebar
sidebar.line: Every page in one quiet list down the side.

grouped.label: Grouped
grouped.line: The same list in named groups, so a page is found by where it lives.

rail.label: Rail that opens
rail.line: Icons until the pointer comes, then the whole sidebar over the page.

search.label: Search first
search.line: A large search above the pages, and rows a little larger.

dock.label: Dock
dock.line: The pages in a dock at the bottom; the status bar moves to the top.

command.label: Command bar
command.line: No list on screen: the page’s name at the top opens every page.

pinned.label: Pinned
pinned.line: The pages you pin on top, every page below in its group.

tiles.label: Coloured tiles
tiles.line: Each icon in a tile coloured by its group.

tabs.label: Tab bar
tabs.line: Four pages always at the bottom; More raises the rest.

peek.label: Peek
peek.line: A sheet that opens half way on the pages used most; drag it up for all of them.

full.label: Full screen
full.line: The whole screen becomes the menu, in large type.

arc.label: Thumb arc
arc.line: A corner button fans every page out around the thumb.

address.label: Address bar
address.line: A pill at the bottom names the page you are on and grows into the menu.

api.unreachable: Freightdock could not be reached. Is it running?

stream.ended: The connection ended before Docker was finished.

editor.env_help: NAME=value, a line each. Compose fills ${NAME} in the file with them; to hand them to a container as well, give its service env_file: .env.

grants.help: An Environment administrator does everything here. An Operator starts, stops and opens consoles, and makes and removes nothing. Helpdesk reads everything, with no console. A Standard user makes things and manages what is theirs, their teams’ or public. A Read-only user reads only that. A grant on the environment wins over its group’s, a person’s own over a team’s, and of several teams the highest.
grants.no_teams: No teams yet: make them under Users.

ownership.help: Standard and read-only users see what is public, their teams’ and their own; everybody else here sees everything.

block_privileged.label: Privileged mode
block_privileged.help: A privileged container can do everything the host can.

block_bind_mounts.label: Host paths
block_bind_mounts.help: Bind mounts of the host’s folders and files (and volumes that are a host path underneath), but those under the paths allowed below. Named volumes stay.

block_host_pid.label: The host’s processes
block_host_pid.help: pid: host: every process on the host is seen and can be signalled.

block_devices.label: Devices
block_devices.help: Host devices, GPUs and other device requests, and bind mounts of /dev.

block_cap_add.label: Extra capabilities
block_cap_add.help: cap_add, such as SYS_ADMIN or NET_ADMIN.

block_security_opt.label: Security options
block_security_opt.help: security_opt: seccomp, AppArmor, SELinux and no-new-privileges changes.

block_sysctls.label: Sysctls
block_sysctls.help: Kernel settings in the container’s namespaces.

block_consoles.label: Consoles
block_consoles.help: Consoles, attach and commands run in a container, for Operators and Standard users.

security.help: What is switched on here is refused to everybody below Environment administrator on this host: when they make or edit a container, deploy a stack or a template, or a webhook they made runs. Administrators and Environment administrators are never held to it. An edit is held only to what it adds, and updating or recreating a container keeps what it had.
security.bind_allow_help: One absolute path a line: a bind mount under one of these is still allowed while host paths are switched on.
security.inherits: {name}’s settings hold here until this host has its own, which then hold whole.
security.no_group: This host is in no group: without settings of its own, everything is allowed.

swarm.worker: This host is a worker in a swarm. Its swarm is managed from a manager: add that one as an environment.
swarm.no_swarm: This host is in no swarm. Swarm pages are for a host whose Docker manages one (docker swarm init).

webhook.new_address_body: The address there is now stops working; whatever calls it must be given the new one.
webhook.no_sign_in: No sign-in: the address is the key, so keep it like a password.
webhook.copy_now: Copy it now: Freightdock keeps only a hash of it and cannot show it again.
webhook.there_is_one_never: There is one; never called yet.
webhook.there_is_one_by: There is one, made by {by}; last called {when}.
webhook.there_is_one_by_never: There is one, made by {by}; never called yet.
webhook.title: Webhook

setup.title: Welcome aboard
setup.sub: Make the first administrator to start.
setup.password_help: At least 12 characters. This account can do anything to every container.
setup.token_help: On the server: docker exec freightdock freightdock setup-token. It is also in the log (docker logs freightdock), or it is FREIGHTDOCK_SETUP_TOKEN.

notfound.body: This address is not a page of Freightdock. It may have sunk.

login.turn_on_and_sign_in: Turn it on and sign in
login.required: Two-factor is required here. Set it up now to sign in.
login.type_code: Type the code your authenticator app shows for Freightdock.
login.or_directory: or with your password or directory password

two_factor.code_help: From your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.
two_factor.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
two_factor.scan: Scan it with an authenticator app (Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator, 1Password...). If it cannot scan, type this key into it:
two_factor.recovery_keep: Keep them somewhere safe, apart from your phone. Each one signs you in once in place of a code. Freightdock keeps only their hashes and cannot show them again.

volumes.driver_options_help: One name=value a line: type=nfs, o=addr=192.0.2.5,rw, device=:/export.

remove_used.one: {count} container mounts it: Docker will not remove it until they are gone.
remove_used.other: {count} containers mount it: Docker will not remove it until they are gone.

volumes.empty_text: Containers make their own, or make one here.
volumes.prune_body: Volumes no container mounts go, with their data.
volumes.prune_all_help: Not only anonymous volumes: every one no container mounts.
volumes.sub: Where containers keep what must outlive them.

networks.internal_help: No way out to the internet.
networks.attachable_help: Containers can join it by hand (overlay networks).
networks.disconnect_body: It loses its address on this network until it joins again.
networks.aliases_placeholder: other names on this network, comma between
networks.remove_used: Containers are on it: Docker will not remove it until they leave.
networks.prune_body: Networks of your own that no container is on go.
networks.sub: How containers reach each other and the world.

events.sub: What Docker does, as it does it, from an hour ago on.

dashboard.nothing_happened: Nothing has happened in the last hour.
dashboard.sub: Everything on this host, at a glance.

prune.title: Clean up Docker
prune.body: Stopped containers, networks no container uses, untagged images and the build cache go.
prune.volumes_stay: Volumes stay unless you say otherwise below: they hold data.
prune.all: Every unused image and volume too
prune.all_help: Images no container uses, tagged or not, and every volume no container mounts.

containers.remove_running: It is running: it will be stopped and removed.
containers.remove_body: The container goes; its image and named volumes stay.
containers.anon_volumes_help: Volumes made for it alone, without a name.
containers.recreate_body: It is made again with the same settings, from its image as it is now. Data in named volumes stays; anything written inside the container itself goes.
containers.pull_first_help: For a newer image under the same tag.
containers.empty_text: Make one, or deploy a stack.
containers.prune_body: Containers that are not running go. Their images and volumes stay.
containers.sub: Everything that runs here, and what it is using.

container.on_every_network: It is on every network there is.
container.disconnect_body: It loses its address on this network until it joins again. It keeps running.

verdict.current: Up to date with its registry.
verdict.outdated: A newer image is out under its tag.
verdict.unknown: Nothing to compare: its image was built or loaded here.
verdict.pinned: Pinned to a digest: it never changes.

container.not_checked_yet: Not checked yet: Freightdock looks every quarter of an hour.
container.check_off: The update check is off in Settings.
container.auto_on: It is updated by itself when a newer image is out.
container.auto_off: Automatic updates are off for it.
container.auto_by_label: Automatic updates: on, by its {label} label.
container.auto_switch: Update it by itself when a newer image is out
container.auto_off_everywhere: Automatic updates are off in Settings for every container
container.oom: It was last stopped for using more memory than it may.
container.webhook_what: A POST to its address pulls its image again and recreates the container with the same settings.
container.stopped_logs_end: The container stopped; its logs end here.
container.console_not_running: A console opens inside a running container. Start it first.
container.console_role: A console inside a container can change anything in it: your role here does not open one.
container.attach_closes: Its input closes when an attach lets go (it was started with -i but not kept open), so this only watches: typing could end it.
container.attach_no_input: It was made without an open input (-i), so this only watches what it prints.
container.attach_tty: What you type goes to the main process. Ctrl-C goes to it too and may stop the container; leaving the page, or Ctrl-P Ctrl-Q, lets go and leaves it running.
container.attach_input: What you type goes to its input, without a terminal: nothing is echoed back, and a line is sent with Enter. Leaving the page leaves it running.
container.attach_main: The container’s main process, {cmd}, from now on.

cpu_hint.one: of {count} CPU ({all} is all of them)
cpu_hint.other: of {count} CPUs ({all} is all of them)

history_soon.one: Freightdock samples every running container every second; the first samples show here soon after it runs.
history_soon.other: Freightdock samples every running container every {count} seconds; the first samples show here soon after it runs.

container.history_off: Resource history is off in Settings.
container.no_processes_stopped: A stopped container has no processes.

container_edit.pulled_if_missing: Pulled if it is not here.

more_mounts.one: {count} more mount is set as a Docker mount; it is kept. The JSON tab shows it.
more_mounts.other: {count} more mounts are set as Docker mounts; they are kept. The JSON tab shows them.

container_edit.restart_help: When Docker starts it again by itself.
container_edit.init_help: A tiny init as process 1, which reaps zombies and passes signals on.
container_edit.interactive_help: A terminal and an open input, as docker run -it gives.
container_edit.privileged_help: Everything the host can do. Only for what truly needs it.
container_edit.replace_sub: Saving replaces the container with one made like this; if that fails, the old one stays.
container_edit.new_sub: Docker’s own options, the everyday ones as fields.
container_edit.create_body_help: As the Engine API documents it. What you change here is what is sent.
container_edit.not_replaced: Not replaced. The old container is as it was.

images.load_help: A .tar from docker save, or from Export here.
images.push_help: Registries that need a sign-in come with M3; until then, a public or open registry.

remove_used.one: {count} container uses it. Docker keeps it unless you force it, and then that container keeps running from layers that no longer have a name.
remove_used.other: {count} containers use it. Docker keeps it unless you force it, and then those containers keep running from layers that no longer have a name.

images.remove_body: Its layers go, unless another image shares them.
images.force_help: Remove it even while in use, or with several tags.
images.prune_untagged_body: Images with no tag that no container uses go.
images.prune_all_body: Every image no container uses goes, tagged or not. They can be pulled again.
images.git_help: Docker clones it and builds from there.
images.upload_help: A .tar (or .tar.gz) of the folder to build: the Dockerfile and everything it copies in.
images.no_cache_help: Every step again, from the top.
images.choose_file: Choose the file to build from.
images.build_sub: From a Dockerfile, a folder you upload, or a Git repository.

stacks.empty_text: Write a compose file, deploy a template, or start one from Git.
stacks.sub: Compose projects: Freightdock's, and the ones started elsewhere.
stacks.name_help: The Compose project name: lower-case letters, digits, - and _.
stacks.deploy_now_help: Otherwise it is kept, to deploy from its page.
stacks.where_from: Where the compose file comes from
stacks.new_sub: A compose file and its variables, or a Git repository, deployed with Docker Compose.
stacks.cannot_read: Freightdock does not read its files
stacks.unreadable: {reason} Paste its compose file to adopt it; relative paths in it are then read from the stack's own folder in Freightdock's data.
stacks.adopt_help: This is its compose file as Compose reads it from where it was started, relative paths made absolute. Adopting keeps it as one of Freightdock's stacks; its containers stay as they are until it is next deployed.
stacks.not_started_by: A Compose project Freightdock did not start.

stack.webhook_what: A POST to its address deploys the stack again: from its repository's branch as it is now when it is from Git, its images pulled again (add ?pull=false not to).
stack.remove_body: Its containers and networks are taken down, and the stack and its files go from Freightdock.
stack.remove_volumes_help: The named volumes the stack made, with their data.
stack.deploy_to_fetch: Deploy it to fetch the file.
stack.saved_deploy: Saved. Deploy it to make it so.
stack.docker_error: {reason} Its files can still be read and saved.
stack.env_help: What each service gets when the stack is deployed: its compose file with .env, env_file and the defaults in ${...} filled in.
stack.no_services_body: The compose file has no services.

stack_git.user_help: For a private repository, with a token below.
stack_git.token_kept: There is one. Leave this empty to keep it.
stack_git.token_help: A personal access token with read access. Kept sealed, never shown again.
stack_git.poll_help: 0 to check only when asked (deploy, or the webhook).
stack_git.saved: Saved. The next deploy fetches it.

templates.name_container: The container's; Docker makes one up when it is empty.
templates.name_stack: The stack's: lower-case letters, digits, - and _.
templates.stack_compose: A stack from its compose file.
templates.list_unreadable: A list could not be read
templates.no_lists_text: Add the address of one in Settings.
templates.no_custom_text: Write one: a compose file and the variables it asks for.
templates.sub: Apps ready to run, from Portainer's template lists and your own.
templates.title: Title
templates.vars_help: NAME=default, a line each; a # line just before one is the label it is asked by. They become the stack's .env.
templates.remove_body: The template goes; stacks made from it stay.
templates.custom_sub: A compose file to deploy again and again, and the variables it asks for.

home.older: Older than this Freightdock ({version}): update the agent.
home.no_match_text: Clear the search or a filter to see more.
home.none_text: Setup makes the local one; add more under Environments.
home.none_for_you_text: An administrator gives you a role on a host, or on its group, and it shows here.
home.sub: Every host Freightdock manages. Choose one to work on it.

environments.address_label: Freightdock’s address, as the agent’s host reaches it
environments.address_help: The agent endpoint: this server’s name or address with port 7444 (or what FREIGHTDOCK_AGENT_ADDRESS says). It must be reachable from the agent’s host.
environments.run_here: Run this on the host the agent is for.
environments.token_once: The join token is good once, until {when}, and is not shown again. The agent spends it on a certificate of its own, kept in its volume, and dials Freightdock with that from then on.
environments.tls_help: Docker’s TLS port, as dockerd --tlsverify listens.
environments.ca_help: ca.pem: the CA that signed the host’s certificate.
environments.cert_help: cert.pem: Freightdock’s certificate for the host.
environments.key_kept: Kept. Paste a new one to change it.
environments.key_help: key.pem. Kept sealed; never shown again.
environments.about_agent: The host runs freightdock-agent, which dials out to Freightdock: nothing on it is opened to the network. You get the line that starts it next.
environments.about_tls: Freightdock dials Docker’s own TCP port with a client certificate.
environments.keep_certs: Leave the certificates empty to keep the ones there are.
environments.new_token_enrolled: The agent’s certificate stops working at once and its tunnel is cut: start it again with the new token.
environments.new_token_body: The token given before stops working.
environments.remove_agent: Freightdock forgets the host: the agent’s tunnel is cut and its certificate opens nothing any more. The containers on it stay as they are.
environments.remove_body: Freightdock forgets the host. The containers on it stay as they are.
environments.sub: The Docker hosts Freightdock manages, and how each is doing.

env_groups.one_group: A host is in one group at most.
env_groups.no_groups_yet: There are no groups yet: add one under Groups.
env_groups.tags_help_known: Enter or a comma after each. In use: {known}.
env_groups.tags_help: Enter or a comma after each.
env_groups.description_placeholder: What the hosts in it have in common
env_groups.moves_here: Now in {name}: ticked, it moves here.
env_groups.tag_help: Up to 40 characters, without a comma.
env_groups.remove_group_body: Its hosts stay, in no group.
env_groups.groups_sub: A host is in one group at most; a role given on a group is had on each of its hosts.
env_groups.no_groups_text: Put hosts that belong together in a group.
env_groups.remove_tag_body: It comes off every host that has it.
env_groups.tags_sub: Any number to a host, to find it by.
env_groups.no_tags_text: Give a host tags when you edit it, or add them here.

registries.help_dockerhub: A personal access token (Account settings, Personal access tokens) is better than the password. Signed in, pulls count against your account’s limit, not the address’s.
registries.help_ghcr: A token with read:packages to pull, and write:packages to push.
registries.help_gitlab: A token with read_registry (and write_registry to push). For your own GitLab, give its registry’s address.
registries.help_ecr: An IAM user’s key allowed ecr:GetAuthorizationToken and to pull (and push). Freightdock swaps it for ECR’s 12-hour token as it needs one.
registries.help_quay: A robot account (owner+name) and its token work best.
registries.help_custom: Any registry that speaks Docker’s registry API (Harbor, Nexus, Gitea, registry:2…). Leave the user empty for one without a sign-in.
registries.address_help: The registry’s host, and its port if not 443. Start it with http:// for one on plain HTTP (Docker must allow it as an insecure registry).
registries.region_help: Read from the address when it is ECR’s own (<account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com).
registries.kept: Kept. Type a new one to change it.
registries.added: Added: it answered and took the sign-in.
registries.remove_body: Freightdock forgets the registry and its sign-in. Images pulled from it stay; a pull from it after this goes without signing in.
registries.empty_admin: Add one to pull private images, push, and browse it. Public images pull without one.
registries.sub: Where images come from and go to. Pulls, pushes and new containers sign in to the one an image is on by themselves.
registries.no_tags_text: Nothing has been pushed to it yet.
registries.no_repos_text: Nothing has been pushed to it that this user may see.
registries.help_forgejo: Your Forgejo’s own address: its packages are its registry. An access token (Settings, Applications) with read:package to pull, and write:package to push.
registries.help_gitea: Your Gitea’s own address: its packages are its registry. An access token (Settings, Applications) with read:package to pull, and write:package to push.

swarm.no_services_text: Create one, or deploy a stack.
swarm.no_task_running: No service has a task running now.
swarm.sub: The cluster at a glance: its nodes, services and the tasks they run.
swarm.labels_help: One name=value a line. Placement constraints read them: node.labels.zone == a.
swarm.remove_up: It is still up: run docker swarm leave on it first, or force it out here and it is forgotten while it runs.
swarm.remove_down: It is down: the swarm forgets it. It can join again with a join token.
swarm.force_help: Remove it although it is up.
swarm.paused_done: Paused: no new tasks go to it.
swarm.drain_body: Its tasks stop here and start on other nodes; no new ones come to it until it is active again.
swarm.demote_body: It stops being a manager. Keep an odd number of managers, three or five, so the swarm keeps its quorum.
swarm.nodes_sub: The hosts in the swarm: managers keep its state, workers run its tasks.

swarm_services.command_help: Its arguments, as on a command line.
swarm_services.ports_help: One a line: 8080:80, 8080:80/udp, or 80 for any free port. Every node answers on it.
swarm_services.networks_help: Overlay networks to join, one a line.
swarm_services.placement_help: One constraint a line: node.role == manager, node.labels.zone == a.
swarm_services.spec_help: Everything Docker takes, as its API documents it. What you write here is what is made.
swarm_services.every_node_help: Global: one task on each node, as many as there are.
swarm_services.sub: What the swarm runs: each a count of tasks spread over its nodes.
swarm_services.image_help: Its tasks are replaced one by one, as its update settings say.
swarm_services.replaced: Its tasks are replaced one by one.
swarm_services.roll_back_body: Back to its settings before the last update, its tasks replaced as for an update.
swarm_services.remove_body: Every one of its tasks stops and goes.
swarm_services.mode_global: global, one task on every node
swarm_services.every_task: Every task’s lines together, as they come.
swarm_services.spec_edit_help: Docker’s own, whole. Saving updates the service: its tasks are replaced as its update settings say, and the old spec is kept for a roll back.

secrets.sub: Passwords, keys and certificates, given to services as files under /run/secrets. A value is never shown again.
secrets.value_help: Written once into the swarm, encrypted there; nobody can read it back, here or in Docker.

configs.sub: Files given to services, kept in the swarm: not secret, so their text can be read.

swarm_objects.secret_hidden: Its value is not shown: it went into the swarm when it was made and does not come back out. To change it, make a new one and point the services at it.

remove_used.one: A service uses it: Docker will not remove it until it stops.
remove_used.other: {count} services use it: Docker will not remove it until they stop.

swarm_stacks.empty_text: Deploy a Compose file to the swarm.
swarm_stacks.elsewhere_no_file: deployed elsewhere: Freightdock has no file
swarm_stacks.sub: Compose files deployed to the swarm with docker stack deploy.
swarm_stacks.compose_help: As docker stack deploy reads it: deploy: for replicas, placement and updates; build: is not used. Services no longer in the file are removed.
swarm_stacks.new_sub: A Compose file, deployed to the swarm as services.
swarm_stacks.remove_body: docker stack rm: its services, and the networks, secrets and configs the stack made, go.
swarm_stacks.no_file: It was deployed from somewhere else, so Freightdock has not got its Compose file. Deploying it here once (with the same name) gives it one.

users.password_help: At least 12 characters. They can change it in Account.
users.not_yourself: You cannot take this away from yourself.
users.admin_help: Everything, everywhere. Anybody else has only the roles given to them per environment or group.
users.new_password_help: At least 12 characters. Their sessions end and their API tokens are revoked.
users.disable_body: They are signed out at once and cannot sign in, here or through SSO, until enabled again.
users.reset_totp_body: Their authenticator and recovery codes stop working. They sign in with the password alone, or set up a new authenticator at their next sign-in if two-factor is required.
users.remove_body: Their sessions, API tokens, roles and team places go with them.
users.users_sub: Who may sign in. What each may do on a host is their role there, given under Environments.
users.no_teams_text: Put people in a team to give them a role, or share a container or stack with them, all at once.
users.remove_team_body: Its roles go with it, and what was shared with it is the administrators’ again.
users.teams_sub: Groups of people, given roles and shared things together.
users.sub: Who may sign in, and the teams they are in.

activity.empty_text: What people do in Freightdock shows here.
activity.sub: Who did what, and from where.

signins.nothing_text: Nobody signed in or out that way yet.
signins.sub: Who came in, how and from where.

account.copy_now: Copy it now: Freightdock keeps only a hash of it and cannot show it again. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
account.connect_claude: Connect Claude Code to Freightdock with it:
account.read_only_note: This token is read-only: the agent can look, but every change it tries is refused.
account.ca_intro: Freightdock made its own HTTPS certificate, signed by a certificate authority of its own that lives in its data folder. Trust that CA once and every tool checks Freightdock’s certificate as it should, with no warning to click through.
account.node_tool: Claude Code, and any Node tool
account.whole_machine: Trust it on the whole machine, or in a browser
account.browsers: Chrome, Edge and Safari use the machine’s; Firefox has its own, under Settings, Privacy & Security, Certificates, View Certificates, Authorities, Import (or set security.enterprise_roots.enabled). Trusting it means trusting whatever this Freightdock signs, so keep its data folder to yourself.
account.mcp_off: The MCP server is turned off in this Freightdock: an administrator turns it on in Settings, under AI agents (MCP).
account.signs_in_with_value: An API token, as Authorization: Bearer
account.make_above: Make a token above, then run this with it in place of <token>:
account.agent_may: The agent may do what you may, or only look with a read-only token; every change it makes is in the activity log under the token’s name.
account.connect_agent_sub: Freightdock is an MCP server: an agent such as Claude Code can list, start, stop, inspect and run things in your containers through it, as you.
account.token_name_help: What it is for, so you know which to revoke.
account.read_only_help: It may look at everything you may, and change nothing.
account.revoke_body: Whatever uses it is refused from now on.
account.no_tokens_text: Make one for a script or an AI agent.
account.tokens_sub: For scripts and AI agents. A token acts as you; the activity log says which one made a change.
account.new_one_help: At least 12 characters. You stay signed in here; everywhere else you are signed out, and your API tokens are revoked.
account.sso_sub: Sign in to this account through a provider as well as with its password. An account is linked to one provider.
account.linked: Linked: the provider signs you in to this account from now on.
account.via_provider: You sign in through a provider, whose own two-factor applies.
account.required_next: Two-factor is required here: you will be asked to set it up at your next sign-in.
account.totp_intro: After your password, a six-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone. A password that leaks is then not enough.
account.few_codes: Few recovery codes left: make new ones.
account.old_stop: The ones you have stop working.
account.password_alone: Your password alone signs you in again.
account.two_factor_sub: A code from your phone after your password.
account.sub: Who you are signed in as, your password, two-factor, and your API tokens.
account.role_per_host: Your role on each host, given by an administrator
account.language_sub: The language Freightdock speaks in this browser. What the server says when something fails stays in English.
account.bad_redirect: The sign-in provider gave an address Freightdock will not follow.
account.linked_to: Linked: {name} signs you in to this account from now on.
account.signs_in_ldap: Signs in with a password checked by {name}

settings.defaults: Every choice at its default: FinUI as it ships.
settings.saved_everybody: Saved. Everybody sees it on their next page.
settings.appearance_sub: How Freightdock looks, for everybody on it
settings.preset_help: A code made at FinUI create: colours, corners, density and more. Paste the code, or the address or install line that holds it.
settings.template_lists_help: The address of a list in Portainer's template format (v2 or v3), one a line. Portainer's own is {default}.
settings.templates_sub: Where the Templates page reads them from
settings.every_s_help: 10 to 3600. A sample of every running container on every host.
settings.history_help: Keep what each container uses, for the History tab on its page.
settings.history_sub: CPU, memory, network and disk over time
settings.check_hours_help: 1 to 168. What a registry said is kept until then, so Docker Hub’s limits are never near.
settings.look_newer_help: Compare every container’s and image’s tag with its registry, for the update badges.
settings.auto_help: Update the containers that opted in (the freightdock.auto-update=true label, or the switch on their page): pulled, made again with the same settings, and put back if the new one does not stay up.
settings.updates_sub: Newer images under the same tag

mcp_off_body.one: Every AI agent that uses it is refused from now on ({count} active token), until it is turned on again. The tokens stay good for the API.
mcp_off_body.other: Every AI agent that uses it is refused from now on ({count} active tokens), until it is turned on again. The tokens stay good for the API.

settings.revoke_body: Whatever uses it is refused from now on. They can make a new one in Account.
settings.no_tokens_text: Each person makes their own in Account.
settings.mcp_sub: Freightdock as an MCP server, for Claude Code and other agents
settings.mcp_help: Let AI agents in at /mcp with an API token, for the whole of this Freightdock. Off, /mcp refuses everybody; the tokens still work for the API.
settings.connect_claude: Connect Claude Code with a token in place of <token>:
settings.own_token: Make your own token in Account
settings.each_person: Each person makes theirs there; a token acts as its owner.
settings.migrate_sub: Read through its API; nothing in Portainer changes
settings.migrate_body: Bring Portainer’s stacks (adopted in place, their containers kept), Git stacks, groups, tags, registries and custom templates into Freightdock.
settings.sub: How Freightdock looks, how it lets people and AI agents in, what it keeps, and where app templates come from.

signin_settings.google_help: APIs & Services, Credentials: make an OAuth client ID of the kind Web application, with this as an authorized redirect URI. Google sends no groups: name the e-mail domains that may come in.
signin_settings.entra_help: App registrations, New registration: a Web redirect URI of this, then a client secret under Certificates & secrets. Put your tenant ID in the issuer. For groups, add the groups claim under Token configuration; Entra sends their object IDs, which are what the group lists below take.
signin_settings.github_help: Settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps (an organization’s, or yours): New OAuth App with this as the callback URL. The groups are your organizations (my-org) and teams (my-org/admins); the organization must allow the app (third-party access).
signin_settings.ldap_help: People sign in with their directory name and password in the usual form. Freightdock searches as the service account (read only is enough), then checks the password by binding as the person.
signin_settings.authentik_help: Make an OAuth2/OpenID provider, Confidential, with this redirect URI set to strict and only the authorization code and refresh token grants. Make an application for it, and bind it to the groups that may come in. The issuer is then https://<authentik>/application/o/<slug>/.
signin_settings.id_help: In its addresses: a to z, 0 to 9 and -. It cannot be changed later.
signin_settings.on_ldap: Check passwords typed in the sign-in form against this directory too.
signin_settings.on_oidc: Show its button on the sign-in page.
signin_settings.label_ldap: As the activity and auth logs name it.
signin_settings.label_oidc: The button reads Sign in with this.
signin_settings.github_address_help: https://github.com, or your GitHub Enterprise server.
signin_settings.issuer_help: The provider’s OpenID configuration URL without /.well-known/openid-configuration.
signin_settings.name_claim_help: The claim a person’s Freightdock name is taken from.
signin_settings.group_filter_help: {dn} is the person’s DN, {username} the name typed; both escaped. Active Directory’s member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:= follows nested groups.
signin_settings.starttls_help: For an ldap:// address: TLS before anything is sent.
signin_settings.allow_plain_help: No TLS at all: every password crosses the network as typed. Only on a network you trust; the activity log notes it.
signin_settings.ca_help: PEM. Trust this CA for the directory’s certificate instead of the system’s.
signin_settings.bind_password_help: Kept sealed; never shown again. Changing the address asks for it again.
signin_settings.user_filter_help: {username} is the name typed, escaped so it cannot change the filter.
signin_settings.id_attr_help: What a person is kept by when their name or place changes: entryUUID, or objectGUID in Active Directory.
signin_settings.admin_groups_github: Organizations or teams (org/team) whose members are administrators.
signin_settings.admin_groups_help: Members of any of these are administrators, set again at every sign-in. With none, a sign-in never changes anybody’s role.
signin_settings.user_groups_help: Members of any of these may sign in, with the roles given to them per host or group. With both lists empty, everybody the provider lets through may.
signin_settings.domains_help: When any: only a person whose verified e-mail address is at one of these comes in.
signin_settings.link: Sign in to the local account with the same name
signin_settings.link_help: A person’s first sign-in lands in the local account of their name, if no one is linked to it yet. Off if people choose their own names there.
signin_settings.teams_on_help: At every sign-in, put people in the teams their groups map to, and out of the ones this provider put them in that they no longer map to. Teams given by hand stay.
signin_settings.teams_make: Make teams that are not there
signin_settings.teams_make_help: Otherwise a rule waits until an administrator makes its team.
signin_settings.team_rules_help: One a line: a group, -> and a team. A group between slashes is a regular expression whose captures the team may use ($1).
signin_settings.test_user_help: A name to look up; with a password, it is checked too.
signin_settings.not_found: Not found (or found more than once)
signin_settings.remove_body: Its button goes, and nobody signs in through it any more. Its people keep their accounts; those with no password can only come in another way.
signin_settings.none_yet: None yet. Passwords are the only way in.
signin_settings.providers_sub: Single sign-on and directories, besides the local passwords, which always keep working.

without.one: {count} person signs in with a password and no second factor yet; they set one up at their next sign-in.
without.other: {count} people sign in with a password and no second factor yet; each sets one up at their next sign-in.

signin_settings.tf_optional: Two-factor is up to each person.
signin_settings.tf_sub: A code from an authenticator app after the password: local accounts and directories. Single sign-on has its provider’s own.
signin_settings.required_all_help: Every sign-in with a password asks for a code; somebody without an authenticator sets one up then. An administrator can reset a lost one under Users.

events.container_died: A container stops on its own: it crashed, or ran out of memory
events.update_available: A newer image is out for a container
events.environment_down: An environment stops answering: an agent's tunnel ends, a host goes away

notifications.webhook_help: Freightdock POSTs a JSON body here: event, title, message, environment, target, at.
notifications.signing_help: Optional. With one, each request carries X-Freightdock-Signature: sha256= the HMAC-SHA256 of its body.
notifications.ntfy_token_help: Optional: for a topic that needs one (tk_...).
notifications.on_help: A channel that is off is told nothing; its test still works.
notifications.added: Added. Send it a test to see it works.
notifications.empty_text: Add a webhook, e-mail, ntfy or Gotify to hear when a container dies, an update is out or a host goes down.
notifications.sub: Where Freightdock tells you when something needs you.

backups.keep_help: Archives kept there, 1 to 365; the oldest beyond go.
backups.passphrase_help: Seals every archive. Freightdock keeps it sealed for the schedule, but a restore asks for it: keep it somewhere other than this server.
backups.folder_help: On Freightdock’s side: mount a volume or a share there. Empty is the data folder’s backups/.
backups.bucket_help: Made when it is not there.
backups.vhost_help: bucket.endpoint/key rather than endpoint/bucket/key. AWS takes both; most others want the second.
backups.schedule_help: The database (copied while Freightdock runs), secret.key, the agents’ CA, the TLS certificate and the stacks’ files.
backups.settings_sub: Freightdock’s own data, sealed with your passphrase
backups.starting_again: Freightdock is starting again with the backup in place…
backups.restore_warning: Everything Freightdock keeps goes back to how it was in {name}: users, environments, settings, the activity log. What is there now is moved aside in the data folder, not deleted. Containers are not touched.
backups.drop: Drop a backup here to restore it
backups.drop_help: A .backup Freightdock made, here or on another server, up to 1 GB.
backups.cli: With Freightdock stopped, the same is: freightdock restore <file> (the passphrase from FREIGHTDOCK_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE, or typed), then start it.
backups.no_archives_text: Back up now, or turn the schedule on.
backups.asked_next: You are asked for its passphrase next.
backups.sub: Freightdock’s own data, sealed and kept where you say.

portainer.address_help: The address Portainer answers at, as Freightdock reaches it. Behind a browser check (Cloudflare and the like) the API is not reachable: use the inside address.
portainer.token_help: In Portainer: My account, Access tokens, Add access token, as an administrator. Freightdock keeps it sealed and only ever reads with it.
portainer.cert_help: For a self-signed Portainer: paste its certificate (or the CA that signed it) and Freightdock trusts that one. openssl s_client -connect host:9443 -showcerts prints it.
portainer.skip_help: Anyone between Freightdock and Portainer could then read the token. Pasting the certificate is better. The choice is written in the activity log.
portainer.connected: Connected: Portainer answered and took the token.
portainer.nothing_ticked_text: Tick what to bring over, then import.
portainer.new_agent_body: Freightdock makes an agent environment by that name and shows the line that starts its agent on that host. Once the agent has dialled in, read Portainer again and its stacks can come.
portainer.env_sub: Matched by their Docker engine’s ID, else by name or address. Change any that are wrong.

stacks_sub.one: {can} can come of {count}. Adopted in place: same project name, containers kept.
stacks_sub.other: {can} can come of {count}. Adopted in place: same project name, containers kept.

portainer.group_line: A group; {members} put in it (one already in a group stays there).
portainer.registry_line_password: {kind} at {host}, as {user}: give its password afterwards, Portainer does not give it out.
portainer.team_exists: Freightdock has a team by that name: used.
portainer.team_imported: Imported already: only members it lacks are added.
portainer.members_none: Left out, no Freightdock user of that name: {names}
portainer.nobody_in_it: Nobody is in it in Portainer.
portainer.teams_sub: Made in Freightdock, or matched by name, with the members Freightdock has a user of the same name for. Nobody is made a user, and nobody is taken out of a team.
portainer.keep_people: Also keep a copy of Portainer’s {users} and {teams} as Portainer has them
portainer.people_help: Written down in Freightdock’s settings only; nobody is made a Freightdock user.
portainer.deploy_each: Deploy each stack from Freightdock once it is imported
portainer.deploy_each_help: Off, the containers stay exactly as they are until you deploy. On, Compose recreates what its file differs on.
portainer.unreadable: Some of Portainer could not be read
portainer.sub: Bring over Portainer’s stacks, groups, tags, registries, templates and teams. Portainer is only read: nothing there changes.
portainer.forget_body: Freightdock forgets its address and token. What was imported stays, and so does the record that keeps a second import from making it twice.
portainer.not_checked: Portainer’s certificate is not checked, as chosen. Paste it under Change to have it checked.

volume_files.drop_help: Into {dir}. Up to 256 MB each; a file of the same name is replaced.
volume_files.folder_help: Made in {dir}. Slashes make the folders between too.
volume_files.delete_folder: This deletes the folder {name} and everything in it from the volume {volume}, for good.
volume_files.delete_file: This deletes {name} from the volume {volume}, for good.
volume_files.admins_only_text: A volume’s files are whatever its containers keep, secrets included.
volume_files.truncated: This folder holds more than 5000 entries; the first 5000 are shown.

changelog.sub: What changed in Freightdock, newest first.

cluster.sub: The Freightdock cluster this Freightdock is the UI of.
cluster.not_connected_text: Set FREIGHTDOCK_CLUSTER_API to a manager's admin API to show its cluster here.
cluster.no_nodes_text: Add a node to run workloads on it.
cluster.workload_help: The name the cluster knows this container by.
cluster.remove_body: Its certificate opens nothing more and its stream is cut. To come back it needs a new join token.
cluster.worker_token_text: Put this in /etc/freightdock/worker.env on the new node, with FREIGHTDOCK_MANAGERS set to this manager.
cluster.manager_token_text: Put this in /etc/freightdock/manager.env on the new manager, with FREIGHTDOCK_MANAGER_JOIN set to this manager.
cluster.token_once: It works once and is not shown again.
cluster.labels_help: One key=value a line. They go over the worker's own labels of the same key, and stacks place their workloads by them (node.labels.<key> in deploy.placement).
cluster.authorize_body: It came back fenced and runs no managed workload until it is authorized. Authorize it only when nothing it ran has been started elsewhere in the meantime.

cluster_stacks.title: Cluster stacks
cluster_stacks.sub: Compose stacks the cluster runs, spread over its nodes and kept running by the managers.
cluster_stacks.none_text: Deploy one from a Compose file; the managers place its containers on the nodes.
cluster_stacks.recoveries_sub: Workloads the managers moved off a fenced node, or left there and why.
cluster_stacks.remove_body: Its containers are removed from every node. Named volumes stay.
cluster_stacks.name: Name
cluster_stacks.name_help: 1 to 40 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit.
cluster_stacks.compose_help: image, command, environment, labels, ports, volumes and deploy.replicas are used; anything that would change what runs and is not supported yet is refused by name.

terminal.label: Console
terminal.watching: watching only: what is typed does not reach it
